subject: Data Structures

intro.en: A binary search tree keeps data sorted in a tree shape so that searching, inserting and deleting can be fast.
intro.ru: Binary search tree data ko tree ki shakal mein tarteeb se rakhta hai taake search, insert aur delete tez ho sakein.

definition.en: A binary search tree (BST) is a binary tree in which every key in a node's left subtree is smaller than the node's key and every key in its right subtree is larger.
definition.ru: Binary search tree (BST) aisa binary tree hai jis mein har node ke left subtree ki har key us node ki key se chhoti aur right subtree ki har key bari hoti hai.

explanation.en: To search, compare the key with the root and go left if it is smaller or right if it is larger, repeating until the key is found or a null child is reached. Insertion follows the same path and adds the new key as a leaf. Deleting a node with two children replaces it with its in-order successor (the smallest key in its right subtree). All of these take O(h) time where h is the height: O(log n) for a balanced tree but O(n) for a skewed tree (e.g. inserting sorted data). Self-balancing trees such as AVL and red-black trees keep h = O(log n). An in-order traversal (left, node, right) visits the keys in sorted order.
explanation.ru: Search ke liye key ko root se milayein: chhoti ho to left, bari ho to right jayein, aur yahi dohrayein jab tak key mil na jaye ya khali child aa jaye. Insertion isi raste par chal kar nayi key ko leaf ke taur par lagati hai. Do children wali node delete karne ke liye use in-order successor (right subtree ki sab se chhoti key) se badla jata hai. Yeh sab O(h) waqt lete hain jahan h height hai: balanced tree mein O(log n) lekin skewed tree (maslan sorted data insert karna) mein O(n). AVL aur red-black jaise self-balancing trees h = O(log n) rakhte hain. In-order traversal (left, node, right) keys ko tarteeb se dikhata hai.

example.en: Insert 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80. Root 50; 30 goes left; 70 right; 20 left of 30; 40 right of 30; 60 left of 70; 80 right of 70. Searching 60: 60 > 50 go right to 70, 60 < 70 go left, found in 3 comparisons. In-order traversal: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80.
example.ru: 50, 30, 70, 20, 40, 60, 80 insert karein. Root 50; 30 left; 70 right; 20, 30 ke left; 40, 30 ke right; 60, 70 ke left; 80, 70 ke right. 60 search: 60 > 50 to right 70 par, 60 < 70 to left, 3 muqablon mein mil gaya. In-order traversal: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80.

subject: Databases

intro.en: Normalization is how database designers organise tables so that the same fact is not stored in many places, which avoids inconsistent data.
intro.ru: Normalization ke zariye database designers tables ko aise tarteeb dete hain ke ek hi baat kai jagah save na ho, taake data be-rabt (inconsistent) na ho.

definition.en: Normalization is the process of decomposing relational tables, guided by functional dependencies, to reduce redundancy and avoid insertion, update and deletion anomalies.
definition.ru: Normalization functional dependencies ki rehnumai mein relational tables ko chhote tables mein todne ka amal hai, taake redundancy kam ho aur insertion, update aur deletion anomalies se bacha ja sake.

explanation.en: A functional dependency A -> B means the value of A determines the value of B. First normal form (1NF): every column holds a single atomic value (no lists). Second normal form (2NF): 1NF and no non-key column depends on only part of a composite primary key (no partial dependency). Third normal form (3NF): 2NF and no non-key column depends on another non-key column (no transitive dependency). Boyce-Codd normal form (BCNF) is stricter: the left side of every non-trivial functional dependency must be a candidate key. The smaller tables are linked again with foreign keys. Over-normalising can slow reads because queries need many joins, so some systems denormalise on purpose.
explanation.ru: Functional dependency A -> B ka matlab hai A ki value B ki value tay karti hai. First normal form (1NF): har column mein ek hi atomic value (lists nahi). Second normal form (2NF): 1NF aur koi non-key column composite primary key ke sirf ek hisse par munhasir na ho (partial dependency nahi). Third normal form (3NF): 2NF aur koi non-key column doosre non-key column par munhasir na ho (transitive dependency nahi). Boyce-Codd normal form (BCNF) zyada sakht hai: har non-trivial functional dependency ka baayan hissa candidate key ho. Chhote tables foreign keys se dobara jore jate hain. Zyada normalisation reads ko dheema kar sakti hai kyunki queries ko bohat se joins chahiye, is liye kuch systems jaan boojh kar denormalise karte hain.

example.en: Table Enrollment(student_id, course_id, student_name, course_title, instructor, instructor_office) with key (student_id, course_id). student_name depends only on student_id and course_title only on course_id: partial dependencies, so it is not 2NF. Split into Student(student_id, student_name), Course(course_id, course_title, instructor, instructor_office) and Enrollment(student_id, course_id). In Course, instructor_office depends on instructor (a non-key column): a transitive dependency, so split again into Course(course_id, course_title, instructor) and Instructor(instructor, instructor_office) to reach 3NF.
example.ru: Table Enrollment(student_id, course_id, student_name, course_title, instructor, instructor_office), key (student_id, course_id). student_name sirf student_id par aur course_title sirf course_id par munhasir hai: partial dependencies, yaani 2NF nahi. Todein: Student(student_id, student_name), Course(course_id, course_title, instructor, instructor_office) aur Enrollment(student_id, course_id). Course mein instructor_office instructor (non-key) par munhasir hai: transitive dependency, is liye 3NF ke liye mazeed todein: Course(course_id, course_title, instructor) aur Instructor(instructor, instructor_office).

key_concepts.ru: A -> B: A, B ko tay karta hai.

key_concepts.ru: Redundancy se paida hone wale insertion, update aur deletion masail.

key_concepts.ru: Key ke hisse par (2NF torti hai) vs non-key column ke zariye (3NF torti hai).

code_explanation.en: The instructor's office is stored once in the Instructor table (3NF), not in every course row.
